fixes.explanation: Jesus finishes the list with “…and love your neighbor as yourself.” Say it with me: even the neighbor whose leaf blower fires up at 7 a.m. Jesus doesn't add that part, that's just me having fun. The list that started with “Do not murder…” lands right on loving your neighbor.

The young man says, “All these I have kept…” I think that's a man who feels pretty sure of himself. I once told my oven timer I'd never scorch another batch, and the timer just stayed quiet. Then he asks Jesus another question, and that's where the story really starts moving.
The text says the young man “…went away in sorrow…” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story. He came up to Jesus with a big question and left with a heavy heart. I think this one hurts.

Jesus says, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” He's answering a question about who can be saved. It puts all the weight on God, not on us. That's good news for anybody who feels like the job is too big to do alone.
